summary: Steel-tower lookout on the Flathead Reservation, erection begun by the Indian C.C.C. department in 1939 (firelookout.com says 1935); gone by 1993.

facts.design: Steel tower with an eight-foot square cabin on top (CSKT). firelookout.com gives an 80-foot steel tower with a frame cabin; a 1939 newspaper item described 50-foot steel towers.
facts.status_note: Listed as gone. firelookout.com dates the loss to 1993; the Montana lookouts page lists it as removed.

staffing.status: Staffed in 1979 (Flathead Courier item quoted on the Montana lookouts site). CSKT says it is no longer in use.

access.note: Site lies on the Flathead Indian Reservation; no source gives visiting rules.

visit.trail_note: About 15 miles northwest of Polson (CSKT). A 1960 survey station description puts it about 7 miles southwest of Elmo on a high east-west ridge.

facts.agency: Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes (Flathead Reservation)

events.note: Erection of two 50-foot steel towers began in May 1939 (newspaper item dated May 3, 1939, quoted on Montana lookouts site); expected completion about July 1. firelookout.com dates the lookout to 1935.
July 12, 1979 item: Kathy Felsman of Arlee at the Irvine Lookout, who had spent seven years working in the towers
firelookout.com gives Gone 1993; cause and method not stated

evidence.supports: Steel tower, frame cabin, 80 ft, dated 1935, gone 1993
Site on the Flathead Indian Reservation
Distance 14 miles WNW of Polson (CSKT says 15 miles NW)
Location about 15 miles NW of Polson in Lake County
evidence.quote: Located 15 miles NW of Polson in Lake County, Montana

evidence.supports: Steel tower with an eight-foot square cabin on top
evidence.quote: this lookout was a steel tower with an eight-foot square cabin perched on top.
When it was in service, the person operating the lookout had to scramble down from the steel tower each time a thunderstorm came rolling in.

evidence.supports: May 1939 erection by the Indian C.C.C. department, two 50-foot steel towers
evidence.quote: Work was started this week by the Indian C.C.C. department on the erection of two 50-foot steel tower lookouts in this section.

evidence.supports: One of the two towers on the Irvine Flats section
evidence.quote: One is being erected on the Irvine Flats section and the other on the north side of the Big Draw section.

evidence.supports: Roads built the year before; telephone lines to follow
evidence.quote: Roads to the two lookout sites were constructed last year and after the completion of the lookout stations, telephone lines will be installed.
It is expected that work on the lookouts will be completed about July 1.
Kathy Felsman, Arlee, is presently at the Irvine Lookout and has been working in the towers for seven years.
LOCATED ABOUT 7 MI. SW. OF ELMO, MONTANA, ABOUT 3 MI. S. OF STATE

evidence.supports: Station on a high east-west ridge
Listed as a tower, gone, under the name Irvine Lake

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 1935; a May 1939 newspaper item quoted on the Montana lookouts site shows erection starting in 1939. The story uses 1939 for the start of construction and reports the 1935 date.
The firelookout.com page title says Irving; its own heading and the other sources say Irvine. The story uses Irvine. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list calls the site Irvine Lake.
firelookout.com gives 14 miles WNW of Polson; CSKT gives 15 miles NW. The story says about 15 miles northwest and cites both pages.

corrections.why: The CSKT page and firelookout.com only place the site on the Flathead Indian Reservation. Neither gives visiting rules, and no page read says permission is required.

sources.title: Fire Lookouts
sources.publisher: Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes, Division of Fish, Wildlife, Recreation, & Conservation

notes_for_editor: Elevation: the record's 459.6 m matches CSKT's 1508 ft; firelookout.com gives 5500 ft. Not resolved, so no elevation field was added. Height: the record's 15.2 m matches the 1939 50-foot plan; firelookout.com says 80 ft. height_m omitted because the sources conflict. The record's access 'permission' has no source among the pages read; see corrections. The 1935 and 1939 start dates are both sourced and the story reports both. The 1960 USGS survey station description is on the montanalookouts page, which is the only source for the Elmo location and the east-west ridge. Edits 2026-10-10: 'after seven years' corrected to 'who had spent seven years in the towers' (the 1979 item says she had been working in the towers for seven years as of July 1979); the 1960 USGS description, the 1979 Courier item and the May 3, 1939 date were added to the evidence; the Forest Fire Lookout Association's 'Irvine Lake' name is now stated; the 14-vs-15-mile distance conflict is recorded.
